resharper_align_multiline_expression_braces #

Align a wrapped braced expression with its opening brace. Not read by the C# formatter — one of the unprefixed spellings this export writes for the C++ and VB formatters. Measured at both values on a file with five wrapping initializers: the oracle returns it byte-identical. Negative control on the same file: resharper_csharp_wrap_object_and_collection_initializer_style = chop_always and resharper_wrap_array_initializer_style = chop_always both rewrite it, so the file can show an initializer moving. ⚠ Re-confirmed at the coverage pass on a second probe — an eighteen-file corpus including constructs/wrapping/initializers.cs — where true returns every file byte-identical while resharper_csharp_align_multiline_array_and_object_initializer = true rewrites the initializers in the same run.

Typetrue / false

resharper_expression_braces #

Where a break may land relative to an initializer's braces. Not read by the C# formatter. Measured at all four values on a file whose initializers wrap and whose } therefore sits on a line of its own — the shape a ParenthesesIndentStyle key would move — and the oracle returns it byte-identical each time, while the C# initializer wrap keys rewrite the same file. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified duplicate spelling. ⚠ Partially verified. Flat at all four values on a chopped object initializer, which agrees with the recorded reading — but the positive control did not reproduce here: the C# spelling resharper_csharp_use_continuous_indent_inside_initializer_braces came back SPURIOUS on the same fixture (Skala moved, the oracle did not), so this row still leans on the control recorded against resharper_align_multiline_expression_braces rather than on one established in this pass.

resharper_use_continuous_line_indent_in_expression_braces #

Whether an initializer's contents take a continuation level. Not read by the C# formatter: the C# spelling of this question is resharper_csharp_use_continuous_indent_inside_initializer_braces, which is implemented and observable. Measured at both values with the negative control described on resharper_align_multiline_expression_braces. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified duplicate spelling. ⚠ Partially verified, with the same caveat as resharper_expression_braces: flat at both values on a chopped object initializer, but the C# spelling that should have served as the positive control was itself flat in the oracle on that fixture.

resharper_wrap_braced_init_list_style #

The braced initializer list's wrap style, in the language-generic spelling the export writes. Not read by the C# formatter. ⚠ Probed rather than reasoned about: eleven fixtures under this repository's own .editorconfig, one cleanupcode invocation per configuration, each fixture first shown to move under the key that really governs its construct. Inert at all three values, at 120 and at 60 columns, and with max_initializer_elements_on_line = 10000 and csharp_wrap_array_initializer_style = wrap_if_long in the same run — byte-identical to that run without this key, while resharper_wrap_array_initializer_style = chop_always and resharper_csharp_wrap_object_and_collection_initializer_style = chop_always both chop the same file one element per line. The C# keys are the ones to implement.
